criteria.name: Thumb-stop cover
criteria.notes: The 7-word headline 'Alaska's second wire has a passenger list.' plus 'Data centers aren't on it.' sets up a named tension in huge serif type, and it reads cleanly at the 432 px thumb. There is one focal point, the gold Intertie climbing from Willow into the Range, and Denali and Cook Inlet make it unmistakably Alaskan without cliche. It stops short of 9 because the hook is a metaphor rather than a number. The $150 million sits in the small kicker, and 'passenger list' needs the subline before it lands.

criteria.name: Story arc & swipe momentum
criteria.notes: The beat structure is clear: the hook, then 02 delivering DOE's own reasons at once, then the one wire, the second wire, the bases, a breather, the senator as hinge, the register synthesis and a single ask. The contact sheet reads as one sequence held together by the locator strip and the gold-means-Intertie law. Two things hold it back. 06's 'One corridor. No second path' restates 03's 'One line joins the two halves today' (the same claim, C13), so 03 and 06 are partly interchangeable. The 02 to 05 run is four dense dark plan frames in a row.

criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.notes: The craft cycle lifted it from 7. 03's plan strip is now a full 100 m / 500 m contour field and no longer an empty band. 09's low moon gives the Talkeetna and Chugach fronts real raking light. 01's lowland now has muskeg and taiga variation in place of flat olive. 02's slope-and-aspect hachure, 05's relief stipple and 07's light-weighted engraving are genuine, distinct hands, and 01 is a real GPU PBR DEM render with occlusion, haze and depth blur. It is still short of 8.5. 06, the highest-key frame, reads as smooth grey clay: no visible snow line, no rock texture, a bright halo rim on every skyline, and a stray crisp snowy fragment at the right edge that belongs to a different render. 09's lower-left third is still near-black lumps. 01's right-hand ranges are repeated rounded snow-capped bumps. 08 is a competent table on a plate with almost no modelled art.

criteria.name: Story-art fusion
criteria.notes: The art encodes the story's numbers and geometry. It uses the Intertie's real AEA geometry everywhere, and the 03 profile runs along the line's own length from 0 to 170 miles. 04 puts 170 and 223 miles at one asserted scale and builds the $418M bar from asserted 150 and 268 segments. 05 has exactly 12 unassigned parcel tiles. The focus law draws only what exists as a line and leaves the second wire's stops as unjoined discs. A stranger would read 'a power line between two halves of Alaska' from the art alone. The data center half of the story lives only in type and blue marks, which keeps this off 9.

criteria.name: Alaska authenticity & local relevance
criteria.notes: The deck names places, institutions and people throughout: Beluga, West Susitna, Willow, Healy, Talkeetna, Denali, JBER, Clear, Eielson, AEA, Curtis Thayer, Murkowski and the Alaska Beacon. It is built on the real DEM and real line geometry, and the 'two halves' framing is how the Railbelt talks about itself. One geography wobble an Alaskan could catch: on 01 and 09 the BELUGA ring sits on open inlet water (about x 247, y 2091 at full size), not on the west-side shore by the gas plant.

criteria.name: Insight density & factual weight
criteria.notes: Most frames add a new verified specific. 02 has Wright's verbatim reasons and the absence. 03 has 170 mi and the mid-1980s. 04 has four named stops, 223 mi, $418M/$150M/$268M and Thayer's 'engineering, planning and permitting'. 05 has June 29th, no award and the Beacon's 'most bases'. 07 has the verbatim quote, and 08 sets five records side by side. 06 adds nothing new (C13 again), and 03 is light at 17 words.

criteria.name: Variety vs ledger
criteria.notes: The hero (THE CORRIDOR SURVEY), the noon atmosphere, the 'passenger list' hook and the Instrument Serif over Archivo pairing are all new. Several subsystems repeat No.76 from three days earlier: slope-and-aspect hachure, blue-noise stipple, forget-me-not reserved for the Air Force, and gold on navy for the one live thing. A DEM oblique terrain also recurs. The Air Force lease lane is a running subject for about the sixth time in 30 days.

criteria.name: Legibility & platform fitness
criteria.notes: Mono labels were raised to 24 px for the mobile floor, and body copy is 32 px or larger. Counters are on every frame, the safe zones are respected (the counter was moved to clear 80 px), and the PDF is vector at 4.92 MB with its title. The squeakers: 05's JBER and ANCHORAGE labels are touched by context linework (the qa warn), and 01's DENALI and HEALY labels sit on light horizon haze. All of it still reads at thumb size.

criteria.name: Copy: voice & hook
criteria.notes: The hook is 136 characters and lands inside 140. The caption is 895 characters, right under the 900 ceiling, at 0.93 commas per 100 words, with an analytical voice that takes a position. The deck-summary line is present but clunky ('Today's intertie, the new wire's stops and money, three bases and Murkowski's sentence, then five records, two saying data center.'). The closing question leans rhetorical. Slide 09's 'with data center load in it, or without?' is the better debatable ask.

one_sentence_fix: Replace 06's smooth clay Range with the real DEM rendered with visible rock texture and a hard 1,500 m snow line, and remove the stray crisp fragment at its right edge. The run is at the five-round cap, so this goes to the queue as a lesson rather than an edit, and the next deck should use something other than hachure and stipple for its plan frames.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The Range behind the conductor still reads as airbrushed grey clay: smooth rounded forms with no visible snow line or rock texture, a bright halo rim on every skyline, and a stray crisp snowy fragment from a different render at the right edge (about x 2040 to 2160, y 1660 to 1850 at full size) that breaks the physics of the frame.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Shade the DEM with a slope-gated snow mask (bright snow above 1,500 m and on slopes under 35 degrees, dark rock elsewhere) plus fine-scale normal detail. Drop the skyline rim to the haze value, and crop or regenerate the right edge so a single render fills it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The lower-left third (about x 0 to 1550, y 2230 to 2700 at full size) is still near-black lumps under the moon. The light only reaches the far ranges and the right-hand Chugach front, so the frame's foreground is dead.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Add a moon-blue hemisphere fill of about 0.25 on the near terrain, and let the inlet water carry a faint moon path toward the camera so the Beluga shore and the near hills separate from the black.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The Talkeetna and Chugach ranges on the right read as repeated rounded snow-capped bumps (procedural pillows rather than ridgelines), and the BELUGA ring sits on open water (about x 247, y 2091 at full size) instead of the west shore.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Sharpen ridgelines with a ridged-noise detail pass, or a higher-resolution DEM tile, on the near ranges. Snap the Beluga ring to the coastline point of the gazetteer's Beluga plant.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The register is a clean typographic table on a flat graded plate. Its only modelled event is the lit pool under the plate, so the frame carries almost no artwork weight.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Give the plate real material, such as an engraved or stamped face with a lit bevel and slight relief on the two YES rows, so the synthesis frame has a modelled object and not just ruled rows.
